Question goes like extract only pincodes (plural) and write it to file pincode.csv

If we consider option 1, it will extract pincode but also overwrite the file pincodes.csv
So we end up having 1 pincode in file

if we consider option 4 it is also overwriting the file and not appending, but option 4 is invalid because no standard output is being displayed, but it is doing same job as option 1 extract and write, In question they precisely said extract and write, no mention of standard output
So option 4 and option 1 both should be correct or none of these two should be correct because they are overwriting the file, that option 2 will have different output inside file and option 1 and 4 will have different output, so how can option1 and option 2 correct !!

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Hello @MirzaJunaid

MirzaJunaid:

If we consider option 1, it will extract pincode but also overwrite the file pincodes.csv
So we end up having 1 pincode in file

It seems there’s a small misunderstanding.

The command egrep will extract all matching entries as per regex. So, pincodes.csv will contain all the 6-digit numbers matched from the file.

It extracts all elements that match the regex from all lines, and writes them to the output file.

So,
Option 1 - egrep -o '[0-9]{6}' Pincode_info.csv > pincodes.csv is correct
Option 2 - egrep -o '[[:digit:]]{6}' Pincode_info.csv >> pincodes.csv is also correct

Option 4 - egrep -q '[0-9]{6}' Pincode_info.csv > pincodes.csv is INCORRECT as it has a q flag which is used to suppress the output. So, no output is written to the pincodes.csv.

For such questions, it’s best to try the commands in a terminal. You will get a clarity of the concepts/commands and it will be helpful in your OPPE.

Thanks & Regards,
Swati Jain
